answer: A pigment spiral: each identity's verified work is dyed with a unique pigment that only its own key can produce, and each new piece of work must spiral outward from the last one, stamped in order by a different peer each time, starting from a dark umber base layer that proves the identity has done slow, real work. A fake can forge one stamp, but it cannot forge the whole spiral or borrow another identity's pigment, and a farm cannot share one spiral across a thousand fakes because each spiral needs its own key, its own base layer, and its own chain of distinct witnesses.
